title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is very faint: either a pale first draft or show-through of p.77, which has the same text in clean form. The title is 'Complexe cotangent des groupes de t.m.', i.e. groups of multiplicative type.

Setting: G = D(M), the Cartier dual of M, where M is a 'réseau' over S. Here that means a locally constant sheaf of finitely generated abelian groups, not necessarily torsion-free.

Step 1. Take the canonical flat resolution in two steps: 0 → R → Z[M] → M → 0. Here Z[M] = Z^{(M)} is the free abelian group on the underlying set of M, u([m]) = m, and R = Ker u. R is free because it is a subgroup of a free abelian group.

Step 2. Dualising gives an fppf-exact sequence 0 → G → T → T' → 0, with T = G_m^M = D(Z[M]) and T' = D(R). This resolves G by (generally infinite-dimensional) 'tores'.

Step 3. The 'triangle de transitivité de Mazur–Roberts' is the distinguished triangle for co-Lie complexes attached to a short exact sequence of flat group schemes. It gives ℓ^G ≃ [ω_{T'} → ω_T] = [R ⊗_Z O_S → Z[M] ⊗_Z O_S], concentrated in degrees −1 and 0.

Result (boxed): ℓ^G ≃ M ⊗^L_Z O_S. So H^0 = M ⊗ O_S = ω_G, and H^{-1} = Tor_1(M, O_S), which is nonzero only for torsion in M that is not invertible on S.

The line marked (4) corresponds to the next page's (1.4): if O_S is a Λ-algebra (Λ = Q or Z/nZ), then ℓ^G ≃ (M ⊗^L_Z Λ) ⊗^L_Λ O_S.

Purpose: compute the co-Lie (cotangent) complexes of finite flat and multiplicative group schemes, presumably as an input to deformation theory of Barsotti–Tate groups and crystals. This is the context of Grothendieck's 1970 'Cristaux' work and of Illusie's thesis.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. One subtlety: the canonical resolution uses Z[M] of infinite rank, so T = G_m^M is not of finite type and is not a torus in the strict sense. The formula still holds, since co-Lie complexes of D(free) are ω = free ⊗ O_S. A finite free resolution, available locally, would avoid this. Grothendieck seems to flag the point with the words 'relativement infini(e)' on the next page.
The machine transcription of this page is unreliable. The clean version is on p.77.

ideas.what: Co-Lie complex of a group of multiplicative type D(M) is M ⊗^L_Z O_S, computed via a resolution by tori and the transitivity triangle.
ideas.modern_name: co-Lie complex ℓ^G (Illusie) of a diagonalisable / multiplicative-type group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie, Complexe cotangent et déformations II (1972), ch. VII; Mazur–Roberts (1970) for the transitivity triangle of co-Lie complexes
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Grothendieck's 1970 Montréal lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné'. The full computation is in Illusie's thesis.

ideas.what: Resolving G = D(M) by an exact sequence of tori 0 → G → T → T' → 0, dual to a two-step free resolution of M.
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 Exp. VIII–X material on D(M) uses similar devices.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faint draft of p.77 containing a standard computation, ℓ^{D(M)} ≃ M ⊗^L O_S, that appears in Illusie's published work. There is nothing new.

'M un module [?]' should be 'M un réseau sur S'.
Z^{(M)} is written Z[M] on the clean copy. The maps are v: R → Z[M] and u: Z[M] → M with u([m]) = m, not α.
(2) should read 0 → G → T → T' → 0 with T = G_m^M and T' = D(R).
